      "observations": [
        "Read all 3,716 owned diff lines across 10 paths, including the full added/replaced/removed test hunks, SQL subjects and test manifest. The landing implements flat, conversation, threaded and grouped add/remove notifications. It also makes sortBy await count/selection, chooses a valid default direction, registers a shared mock tree and enables replacement add/remove tests. Removed buffered fill/add/remove test tasks were skipped in the parent; their sparse-cache architecture is not claimed as active new test coverage.",
        "Flat insert/remove callbacks compare actual message fields, mutate the top-level map and clear its flattened cache before count notifications. ForEach deliberately skips sparse slots while asynchronous initial chunks may still be absent; a successful-mutation flag prevents another mutation as iteration continues. Do not mechanically substitute a loop that changes sparse-array or splice/index behavior.",
        "Threaded rows reserve messageCount minus one child slots. Add/remove distinguishes never-loaded sparse children, materialized but collapsed children and expanded children. Conversations retain only one visible row and a count, force date sorting and invalidate that row until its final message disappears. Grouped rows can insert a new group or mutate existing children, with different count deltas for an open final group. Final thread/group removal deletes the matching map entry. Exact original child addition appends without ordering; accepted sortThread/group child sorting and flag-change handling are later phases.",
        "The native add/remove producer filters for a registered listener and matching view, then sends a fresh plain JS snapshot. setTree(null) now calls clearListener(this) before dropping adapter state. The IDL and native implementation accept an optional identity and preserve a different current listener. The actual TreeView replacement setter detaches the old adapter before connecting the new one. Accepted native notification setup later replaces the retained JSContext with AutoJSAPI; that lifetime repair is not this landing.",
        "The four test families directly inspect visible message-ID arrays, root/child counts, open state, text cells, insertion/removal positions and invalidation/count notifications. They cover date/subject directions, new/existing conversations, never-opened/open/reclosed threads and open/closed/new date/text groups. Conversation tests also assert forced date sorting. SQL fixture subjects make those sort cases concrete. No real displayed tree, missed edge case, race or successful test execution follows from reading the mock.",
        "Manual assertion review found new message-less Assert.equal/strictEqual/ok/deepEqual calls in the shared ListenerTree and added mutation cases. The reset failure assertion does have an expected-behavior message. This is a missing-message finding under the direct user requirement, not a complaint about should alone. Newly added try/finally patterns are retained historical test code; the separate current test-writing preference is not used as a review defect.",
        "Checked the new JS getDateGroup against the actual registered SQL DATE_GROUP function and selection consumer. JS uses strict greater-than at local-midnight cutoffs while SQL uses greater-than-or-equal. Exact-midnight classification can therefore differ between incremental updates and initial SQL grouping; the new tests do not assert those exact boundaries. The original native future threshold has a separate microsecond-units issue already covered by existing lesson ed4bbfd…; accepted native code later multiplies by PR_USEC_PER_SEC. No clock, DST or group-placement run was performed. The bounded caller conversion is explicit: addMessage stores Date milliseconds multiplied by 1000; Message returns stored PRTime, and CreateJSMessage divides by PR_USEC_PER_MSEC before creating a Date. The strict/inclusive comparison is conditional on equivalent instants under the same stable local timezone/day; native Date/timezone internals remain unpaired and timezone or clock changes were not tested.",
        "Comments explain reserved child state, notification effects and deferred ordering. The shared listMessages helper uses an index because visible row indices are the contract. A scoped readability suggestion is to extract the repeated sparse top-level insertion loop and separate declaration/comparison/mutation/notification steps with blank lines; preserve early guards and callback order. Existing before-open child-loader comments conflict with the actual toggle caller and are linked to the existing focused lesson rather than duplicated. No broad JavaScript or C++ style rule is learned from this sample.",
        "Full D286607 creation-to-final timeline, all five actual old/current inline bodies and its literal replacement table were read. The reviewer asks to remove stale #threads map entries at multiple sites; the author agrees. Exact landed final thread/conversation/group removal code deletes the corresponding map entries, independently of Done/Not Done badges.",
        "The summary explicitly excludes child ordering and thread/group repositioning. The author acknowledges missing edge cases and says ordering is the next work in the same bug. Original addChild appends; later fixed sortThread and grouped child sorting remain a separate phase. Sparse initial rows, mock event indices and active changed test assertions were inspected directly; historical completed builds/approval are not a fresh test result.",
        "Reuse exact full primary 1941471 original acc5c6ed… and its prior completed C read in 3557, preserving the original scope/time and immutable record digest. It retains the later add/remove, ordering and listener-lifetime discussion as context, without crediting those separate source phases or rereading a large body for a counter.",
        "Boundary finding is conditional on equivalent timestamps under the same stable local timezone/day. The comm caller conversion is explicit: test Date milliseconds times 1000 into the database, native stored PRTime through Message::GetDate, then PR_USEC_PER_MSEC division before the JS Date. Native date/timezone internals remain unpaired and no clock, DST or actual group-placement experiment ran. Exact predicates and conversions are retained rather than assuming equivalence from function names."
